title: How to Buy a House Without Ever Paying Interest
description:
The three halal home-finance structures explained — Murabaha, Ijara, and Diminishing Musharaka — and the four questions that tell you whether yours is real.

Ten years into a £250,000 mortgage at 5% you have paid £175,377 and you still owe £184,811. You have paid more than you have cleared. Over the full term the interest alone comes to £188,443 — a second house you never get to live in.

This episode shows why the schedule is built that way, what the three halal alternatives actually do differently, and how to check a specific product instead of trusting a label.

Structure descriptions follow standard AAOIFI-style definitions. Some scholars argue certain retail products are conventional lending with extra steps — that criticism is in the video, not hidden. Verify current terms with the provider before signing anything. Education, not financial advice.

Deen & Dinar — no jargon, just mechanisms.
engagement_comment: Question 4 is the one I'd ask first — what happens if you pay late, and where does that money go? A late charge that becomes profit for the bank is riba by another name. What did your bank say?
